items.name: Forearm Plank
items.description: Holding a straight line on your forearms trains the deep core muscles that support your spine.
items.setup: Lie face down, then prop yourself up on your forearms with elbows under your shoulders. Extend your legs behind you with toes tucked under.
steps: Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and gently brace your stomach.
Keep your neck long by looking at the floor just ahead of your hands.
Hold the position, then lower your knees to rest.
items.breathing: Keep breathing slowly – never hold your breath during the hold.
mistakes: Hunching the shoulders up toward the ears.
items.easier: Lower to your knees while keeping a straight line from head to knees.
items.harder: Hold for longer, or lift one foot slightly for a few seconds at a time.
cautions: Stop if you feel lower-back pain; check your hip position or use the knee version.

items.name: Straight-Arm Plank
items.description: A plank on straight arms that builds core strength along with shoulder stability.
items.setup: Start on hands and knees, then place your hands under your shoulders and step your feet back until your legs are straight.
steps: Spread your fingers and press the floor away.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body is straight.
Keep your head in line with your spine.
Hold while breathing steadily, then lower your knees to rest.
mistakes: Letting the chest sink between the shoulders.
items.easier: Hold the plank from your knees, or place your hands on a raised surface.
items.harder: Add slow, alternating shoulder taps without rocking the hips.
cautions: Use fists, or switch to the Forearm Plank, if your wrists are uncomfortable.

items.name: Side Plank
items.description: Balancing on one forearm on your side strengthens the sides of your core and hips.
items.setup: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and your legs straight and stacked.
steps: Press your forearm into the floor and lift your hips.
Form a straight line from your head to your feet.
Keep your top hip stacked above the bottom hip.
Hold, lower with control, and then switch sides.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag toward the floor.
items.easier: Bend your knees and lift your hips from your knees instead of your feet.
items.harder: Raise the top leg slightly, or hold for longer.
cautions: If it causes shoulder pain, try the bent-knee version or skip it.

items.name: Dead Bug
items.description: A slow, controlled exercise lying on your back that teaches you to keep your trunk steady while your arms and legs move.
items.setup: Lie on your back with your arms reaching toward the ceiling and your knees bent at 90 degrees above your hips.
steps: Gently press your lower back toward the floor and brace your core.
Slowly lower your right arm overhead and straighten your left leg toward the floor.
Go only as far as you can without your lower back arching.
Return to the start and repeat on the other side. Each side counts as one repetition.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you extend and in as you return.
mistakes: Arching the lower back off the floor.
items.easier: Move only the legs or only the arms, and keep the range small.
items.harder: Move more slowly, pausing for two seconds at full extension.
cautions: Keep the range small if you feel your lower back lifting.

items.name: Bird Dog
items.description: Reaching the opposite arm and leg from hands and knees builds balance and back stability.
items.setup: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Keep your back flat.
steps: Brace your core.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your body.
Hold for a moment without letting your hips tilt.
Return to the start and switch sides. Each side counts as one repetition.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you reach and in as you return.
mistakes: Arching the back to lift the leg higher.
items.easier: Move only the leg or only the arm.
items.harder: Hold each reach for three seconds, or draw the elbow to the knee between reaches.
cautions: Use a mat or towel under your knees.

items.name: Abdominal Crunch
items.description: A small, controlled curl that works the front of the abdominal muscles.
items.setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Place your fingertips lightly behind your ears or cross your arms over your chest.
steps: Gently brace your core.
Curl your head and shoulders off the floor, bringing your ribs toward your hips.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly back down.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and in as you lower.
mistakes: Pulling on the neck with the hands.
Sitting all the way up with momentum.
Tucking the chin tightly to the chest.
items.easier: Reduce the range of the curl and keep your arms by your sides.
items.harder: Hold the top position for two seconds.
cautions: Keep your neck relaxed and support your head lightly if it tires.

items.name: Bicycle Crunch
items.description: A twisting crunch with a pedalling leg action that works the abdominals and obliques.
items.setup: Lie on your back with fingertips lightly behind your ears, knees bent at 90 degrees above your hips, and shoulders slightly lifted.
steps: Straighten one leg while bringing the opposite elbow toward the bent knee.
Rotate through your upper back rather than pulling on your head.
Switch sides in a slow pedalling motion.
Each twist to one side counts as one repetition.
mistakes: Letting the lower back arch as the leg straightens.
items.easier: Keep the straightened leg higher, or move more slowly.
items.harder: Hold each twist for two seconds.
cautions: Keep your lower back in contact with the floor.

items.name: Reverse Crunch
items.description: Curls the hips toward the chest to work the lower part of the abdominals.
items.setup: Lie on your back with arms by your sides, palms down, and knees bent at 90 degrees above your hips.
steps: Brace your core.
Curl your hips off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest.
Pause briefly.
Lower your hips slowly back down without letting your feet drop.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you curl up and in as you lower.
items.harder: Slow the lowering phase to three seconds.
cautions: Stop if you feel strain in your lower back.

items.name: Hollow Body Hold
items.description: A challenging hold that trains the whole front of the core to keep the lower back pressed down.
items.setup: Lie on your back with your arms reaching overhead and your legs straight.
steps: Press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your shoulders, arms and legs a few centimetres off the floor.
Keep your arms beside your ears and your legs together.
Hold while keeping the lower back down, then lower to rest.
items.breathing: Take short, controlled breaths while keeping your core braced.
mistakes: Letting the lower back lift off the floor.
items.easier: Bend your knees, or keep your arms by your sides.
items.harder: Lower your arms and legs closer to the floor while keeping your back down.
cautions: If your lower back arches, bend your knees or raise your legs higher.

items.name: Russian Twist
items.description: A seated twist that works the sides of your core.
items.setup: Sit with knees bent and heels on the floor. Lean back slightly with a straight back and hold your hands together in front of your chest.
steps: Brace your core.
Rotate your upper body to one side, bringing your hands toward the floor beside your hip.
Return through the centre and rotate to the other side.
Each turn counts as one repetition.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you twist and in as you pass through the centre.
mistakes: Moving only the arms instead of rotating the torso.
items.easier: Sit more upright and keep the range small.
items.harder: Lift your feet off the floor, or hold a light dumbbell.
cautions: Skip twisting exercises if they cause lower-back discomfort.

items.name: Superman Hold
items.description: Lifting your arms and legs while lying face down strengthens the back of the body.
items.setup: Lie face down with your arms extended overhead and your legs straight. Rest your forehead on the floor.
steps: Gently squeeze your glutes.
Lift your arms, chest and legs a few centimetres off the floor.
Keep your neck long by looking down at the floor.
Hold, then lower with control.
items.breathing: Keep breathing steadily during the hold.
mistakes: Lifting too high and crunching the lower back.
Lifting the head to look forward.
items.easier: Lift only the arms or only the legs, or lift one arm and the opposite leg at a time.
cautions: Keep the lift small and stop if you feel pinching in your lower back.

items.name: Plank Shoulder Tap
items.description: Tapping each shoulder from a high plank challenges your core to resist twisting.
items.setup: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders and feet slightly wider than hip-width.
steps: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Place the hand back down and repeat with the other hand.
Keep your hips as still as possible. Each tap counts as one repetition.
items.breathing: Breathe steadily, breathing out with each tap.
mistakes: Rocking the hips from side to side.
items.easier: Perform the taps from your knees, or widen your feet.
items.harder: Bring your feet closer together, or slow each tap down.
cautions: Use fists or push-up handles if your wrists are uncomfortable.

items.name: Standing Cross-Body Crunch
items.description: A standing core move that brings each knee toward the opposite elbow – no floor work needed.
items.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and fingertips lightly behind your ears, elbows wide.
steps: Lift your right knee up and across your body.
At the same time, rotate your torso to bring your left elbow toward the knee.
Return to standing and repeat on the other side.
Each knee lift counts as one repetition.
items.breathing: Breathe out as your elbow and knee meet.
items.easier: Lift the knee lower, rotate less, and hold a wall with one hand if needed.
items.harder: Move at a brisk pace while staying controlled.
cautions: Hold onto a wall or chair if your balance is unsteady.
